title: Instability of the undecidable behavior of the spectral gap in 1D
abstract: The problem of determining the existence of a spectral gap in a lattice quantum spin system was previously shown to be undecidable for one [J. Bausch et al., "Undecidability of the spectral gap in one dimension", Physical Review X 10 (2020)] or more dimensions [T. S. Cubitt et al., "Undecidability of the spectral gap", Nature 528 (2015) and Forum of Mathematics Pi, 10 (2022)]. In this work, we focus on the 1-dimensional result, showing that the constructed family with undecidable behavior is extremely sensitive to perturbations. In particular, for any $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists a 1-local, rank 1, perturbation with norm $O(\varepsilon)$, such that the spectral gap problem for the family in [J. Bausch et al., "Undecidability of the spectral gap in one dimension", Physical Review X 10 (2020)] now becomes decidable.
summary: The paper investigates the decidability of the spectral gap problem for 1D quantum spin chains, building on prior work showing it could be undecidable. The authors demonstrate that this undecidability is highly unstable, proving that even an arbitrarily small, local perturbation can simplify the system such that determining if a gap exists becomes a computationally decidable problem.
main_problem: The core problem addressed is determining whether the spectral gap (gapped vs. gapless) for a 1D lattice quantum spin system is decidable, contrasting with previous results showing undecidability.
main_result: The authors show that the previously constructed family of Hamiltonians exhibiting undecidable behavior is extremely fragile; adding any small, local perturbation renders the spectral gap problem decidable.
method: The analysis involves constructing a specific 1-local, rank-1 perturbation and proving that this perturbation disrupts the fine-tuning energy coupling responsible for linking the spectral gap to an undecidable computation.
model_or_system: The system is a 1D lattice quantum spin chain described by nearest-neighbor Hamiltonians. The analysis focuses on perturbing a specific Hamiltonian family previously shown to encode Universal Turing Machine computations.
key_observables: Spectral Gap ($\Delta$), Ground State Energy ($\lambda_0(H_N)$), and the sign of the ground state energy in the thermodynamic limit.
important_parameters: The perturbation strength $\epsilon > 0$, which is shown to be sufficient to restore decidability regardless of its smallness.
main_assumptions: The undecidability proofs rely on boundary-induced structures (like marker symbols) that are sensitive to local perturbations, while the new result assumes a general 1D nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian structure.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates the final spectrum of the perturbed Hamiltonian ($H_{\epsilon}^N$), showing distinct spectral features for both gapped and gapless scenarios.
paper_structure: The paper first reviews the undecidability result from [1], then details the energy amplification mechanism used in that construction, and finally introduces and analyzes a specific small perturbation to prove decidability by checking only up to a finite critical size $w_\epsilon$.
why_interesting: This work directly challenges the robustness of complexity results in condensed matter theory. Showing that undecidable behavior can be eliminated by a simple local term suggests that many theoretical barriers might be artifacts of specific, non-generic constructions.
